newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times page one - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times page one - April 29.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

* Pentagon and Congressional officials said a strategic defense review by the Pentagon could lead to cuts in U.S. troops and a reduction in Air Force and Navy budgets for high-technology jet fighters.
* Texas officials released a jailed member of a militant separatist group in exchange for the freeing of two hostages held captive by the group.
* Astrophysicists said they discovered what seemed to be a large fountain of antimatter spurting upward from the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
* News Analysis: President Clinton's policy towards China is being attacked on Capitol Hill during a year in which he was supposed to get China policy firmly on track.

* Child welfare officials in the United States often try to delay or avoid returning children to potentially negligant or abusive families, contradicting the belief it is best to keep families together.

* New York City teachers' union president Sandra Feldman is the likely candidate to succeed the late Albert Shanker as head of the American Federation of Teachers, according to some board members of the national union.
* Despite good economic trends in Britain, the country's ruling Conservative party is way behind in the polls as it heads into an election.
